title: Clofab X Zfab Kit In Clo Set
description:
Learn how to digitize physical fabrics using CLOFAB in CLO-SET and the zFab Kit.

In this tutorial, we walk you through the complete fabric digitization workflow—from scanning fabric textures and creating seamless maps to generating physical properties and uploading the completed zfab file to CLO-SET.

In this video:
• Accessing CLOFAB in CLO-SET
• Connecting and calibrating the zFab Scanner
• Scanning fabric textures
• Creating seamless texture maps
• Using Auto and Manual tiling modes
• Preparing and cutting fabric samples
• Measuring fabric with the zFab Draper
• Generating physical properties
• Uploading zfab files to CLO-SET

Subtitles are available in:
English, Korean, Spanish, Portuguese, Japanese, French, and Chinese.

Learn more about the zFab Kit:
https://zfabkit.clo3d.com/
transcript: Hi! In this video, we'll introduce the process of converting physical fabric into digital fabric using the CloFab feature in CloSet. In CloFab, you can create high-quality digital fabrics that match real fabrics by using the ZFab kit, a dedicated fabric measurement device, to precisely scan fabric textures and measure physical properties. Even if you don't own the equipment, you can create a digital fabric suitable for practical use simply by entering a fabric image you have on hand along with basic spec information. What's more, since it runs on a web browser, you can quickly digitalize fabrics even without a high-spec PC. Now, let's take a look at how to use CloFab in CloSet. To use the CloFab feature, first, log in with your CloSet account. After logging in, select the group with which you'd like to share the completed ZFab file. There are two ways to work on a fabric and upload it within the group, and I'll show you both. The first method is to start digitizing directly through the CloFab menu. In this case, once the work is complete, you can select a workroom within the group where you have added permission and upload it there. This is recommended when you need to upload fabrics to multiple workrooms. The second method is to first enter a workroom or company library where you have added permission and then start working. If you click the New button at the top of the screen and select Create New Fabric, the resulting ZFab file will be uploaded directly to that workroom. This is recommended when you're uploading fabrics you've worked on consecutively to the same workroom or company library. Here, we'll go ahead and start with the first method we just went over. First, enter the fabric name, supplier, and owner information in order from the top menu. In the upper right area, you'll notice the screen is divided into the Map tab and the Physical Property tab. In general, we recommend creating the map first and then measure the physical property. If you don't need to create a map, you can also move directly to the Physical Property tab and generate just the physical properties. Let's go back to the map tab and look at the buttons. First, the scan with scanner button is used when scanning directly with the closed ZFabKit scanner device. Second, the open map buttons let you import fabric photos taken without connecting any equipments or files previously available. Keep in mind that at your disposal, you don't use the same material or viewershipazo to view spare products and products, so you don't need to import anyoni or you should use previously scanned with the ZIF-F scanner. First, let's click Open Map. When you click the button, a window appears where you can select a file. At this point, to bring in the image for all the maps at once, select them all and click the Open button. Click the map icons in the toggle menu on the left. You can then confirm that the base color, normal, displacement, roughness, and opacity maps have all loaded correctly. This time, let's click the New button to return to the initial screen and then click the Scan with scanner button. When you click the scanner icon, the connection status updates and you can check the current status by the color of the circle. If the light is gray, the installer has not been installed. Click the button to install the installer needed to install the ZIF-F scanner. operate the Z-Fab kit. After installation, be sure to restart your PC. If the light is red, the Z-Fab kit is not properly connected. In device manager, check that the ports and USB camera entries match what's shown on screen. In my case, both the scanner and the draper are connected, so the camera and USB are each listed twice. For detailed troubleshooting steps, please refer to the FAQ section on the Z-Fab kit website. If the light is green, the device is ready to operate. Click the button to move on to the next step. If you are operating the device for the first time, you will need to perform calibration first. I'll show you how to do it. Align the calibration card in the center with the white colored chip facing the upper right, then carefully close the door so the card doesn't shift or move. Then, click the color checker button in CLO-FAB. Calibration takes about 1 to 2 minutes, and the green check button will appear once it's complete. Now, remove the calibration card from the tray, and with the tray completely empty, click the empty button. Once the process is complete, the scan fabric with scanner button will appear and the date of the most recent calibration will be recorded below it. We recommend performing calibration periodically to scan the actual fabrics color and texture as accurately as possible without distortion. This compensates for slight deviations in the device or changes in the surrounding lightening conditions so you can always achieve consistent results. This matters especially if the device has sat unused for a while or has been moved as the scanning environment may have changed. In that case, be sure to click with calibrate to calibrate again. Now, all the preparation for scanning are complete. The maximum size that the device can scan is 32.6 x 21.5mm. 1.6 cm. If the repeating pattern area is large enough, you can also prepare a smaller sample than this. Insert the sample into the scanner, align with the grain direction, and remove any debris or dust from the surface. Then lay it flat without any wrinkles. Click the Scan Fabric with Scanner button in CloFab to start scanning, which takes about 1-2 minutes. Once the scanning process is complete, the base color map image will appear on the screen. At the same time, a setting menu appears on the right where you can adjust several options. In the viewer, you can zoom in or out by scrolling the mouse wheel and pan the view by holding down the wheel. If you like a larger view, click the gear shape button to hide the settings panel on the right. Before creating a seamless texture, if you'd like to save the original scanned image, click the Save Scan Maps button. Then, set the file path and click the Save button. The files are saved as a .zip file so that once unzipped, you can view the original image for each map. Saving the original image is only possible at this stage so if you need them, be sure to save them now. Next, let's begin the tilling process. You can select the mode using the toggle menu at the very top of the Settings panel. Turning this toggle on switches to Auto Mode, which automatically analyzes and finds the most suitable material. The application appears on the icon with the text, the image of this image is highlighted clearly. When the image is highlighted, the image is automatically saved to the Auto Mode. After the customization, suitable repeat area within the specified range. Turning the toggle off switches to manual mode where you specify the repeat area yourself. In auto mode, the analysis method is applied according to the shape of the pattern present in the fabric. The pattern type is automatically detected by default, but you can also change it manually. If the fabric has no distinct patterns or has an irregular one, select the plain irregular option. For patterns that repeat regularly, such as checks, select the repeat option. Since a normal map is required to accurately analyze the pattern type, auto mode is only enabled when the normal map is included. Note that in manual mode, since you specify the area yourself, no separate analysis step is needed, so the pattern type option is automatically disabled. Keep the automatically selected pattern type and select an area by clicking and dragging. For automatic tilling, you will get the most accurate and fastest results when you select an area that contains the repeating patterns four times. Once you've selected an area, the original image on the right side of the screen and the repeated results based on the analysis can be checked in the preview on the left. If you're not satisfied with the result, click and drag to select a different area. The analyze repeat area in the left preview will update again to match the newly selected area. Clicking the show repeat grid icon in the toggle bar on the left of the preview lets you check which area was repeated to create the seamless texture. Let's check whether the selected area is tiled seamlessly across the other maps as well. The toggle menu located in the left preview and the right viewer are linked to each other, so changing a setting on one side will also change the other. If you feel that the brightness of the tile result is uneven, move the equalize slider in the adjustments menu to even out the tone. This time, let's specify the area manually. Turn off the auto mode toggle, then click and drag on the original image on the right to set the area you want to repeat. The selected area is repeated and the edges are automatically blended so it appears seamless. If you like to move the selected area, click and drag the center of the dotted area in the viewer. To fine tune the area more precisely, you can click the points on the four corners and edges to adjust it in more detail. Let's move on to the next step and measure the physical properties of the fabric. If you don't need to generate physical properties, simply click the upload button at the top to complete the process. Here, you can generate the fabric's physical properties using a model trained on a curated selection of real fabric measurements and hundreds of thousands of simulated variations. It offers high accuracy due to a vast database and the model is continuously trained to support a wide range of special fabric types. Even without the Z-Fab Draper device, the model is continuously trained to support a wide range of special fabric types. Even without the Z-Fab Draper device, you can quickly and easily generate physical properties by entering basic information such as the fabric type and composition ratio. This is especially useful in the early design feeding stage when the physical fabric isn't ready or the fabric hasn't yet been finalized. However, since factors such as yarn, weaving method, and finishing also affect the fabric's drape, it may be difficult to achieve a perfect match with the actual fabric's fill. Therefore, if you need an accurate 3D garment review, we recommend using physical properties generated by directly measuring the actual fabric with the Z-Fab Draper. Let's start with how to take measurement using the Z-Fab Draper. Before turning on the measurement with Draper Toggle, check that the disc is properly mounted inside the Draper and that no fabric is placed inside. Then close the device's door and turn the measure with Draper Toggle on. The connection status will update and you can check the current status by the color of the circle. If the light is gray, the installer has not been installed. Click the button to install the installer needed to operate the Z-Fab kit. After installation, be sure to restore your PC. If the light is red, the Z-Fab kit is not properly connected. In Device Manager, check that the ports and USB camera entries match what's shown on the screen. In my case, both the scanner and the Draper are connected so the camera and USB are each listed twice. For detailed troubleshooting steps, please refer to the FAQ section on the Z-Fab kit website. If the light is green, the device is ready to operate. It will start running and begin the initial setup. This setup runs only once, the first time the device's USB is connected. Next, let's prepare the Draper sample and the fabric information. First, let's look at how to cut a 30cm diameter fabric sample using the Z-Fab Cutter, a component of the Z-Fab Draper. Cut the fabric slightly larger than 30cmx30cm and iron it flat without wrinkles. We recommend cutting the fabric to include the selvage so that you can align it with the grain direction. Alternatively, mark the grain direction directly on the fabric. Grab the center handle of the circular plate resting on the base plate, lift it and press it down. and set it aside outside the base plate for a moment. Then pull the guide bar out to open it. Align the grain direction with the marking lines on the cutter, then place the fabric so its right side faces up. However, very stretchy fabrics that lose their shape easily may shift during cutting, resulting in a different size. So when placing the fabric, lay it down slowly and gently so friction with the pad doesn't stretch it. Align the guide bar with the guide bar dock on base plate and lower it so the circular plate sits exactly in the center. Pull the locking pin on the plate dock outward. While holding it in the outward position, attach the plate unit to the plate dock. Once the plate unit is properly seated, release the locking pin so that you are holding to lock it in place. Once it's fixed in position, carefully close the guide bar. With one hand, press down gently on the handle at the center of the circular plate to keep it from shifting or moving during cutting. With the other hand, hold the plate handle and cut the fabric by smoothly rotating it along the outer edge of the circular plate. Rather than applying excessive force, roll the blade with light pressure, repeating several times. Applying too much force may damage the blade unit or bend the blade, resulting in size errors in the sample, so please be especially careful. Use the reference notch, curved into the top and bottom of the circular plate, to mark the grain direction on the fabric with a pen. After cutting, first remove the leftover fabric scraps from the base plate. Once cutting is complete, check that the size matches a 30cm diameter. Most fabrics can be precisely cut within a tolerance of ±3mm. Measure the weight using the dedicated scale included in the draper package. Remove the two cases and set the unit into gram. If you have another scale on hand, you can use it to measure the weight. When measuring with the case placed on the scale, be sure to set the zero point first. Then, since the fabric sample is larger than the scale's measuring plate, fold it before measuring. If the sample becomes wrinkled while weighing, be sure to iron it flat again before the draper measurement. If you already know the fabric's weight in GSM, you can skip the weight measurement process. Next, use a thickness gauge to measure the thickness. Turn on the thickness gauge and make sure it's set to mm. Then lift the lever, place the sample between the plates and release it. Now, let's place the prepared circular sample into the device with the fabric's right side facing up. Position the fabric so that the grain mark aligns precisely with the two arrow marks, inner and outer, on the draper guard. Then close the door. If the size of the fabric sample doesn't match the draper guard, an error may have occurred during the cutting process. Therefore, you will need to double check that the sample was cut to exactly the 30cm diameter specification. Let's go back to Clofac and take a look at the menu. Construction at the top displays the model version used to generate the physical properties. When the model is updated through additional data training, it's listed in the drop-down menu, where you can also view the history. In Type, select the fabric type. If the type you want isn't on the list, choose the closest match available. When there are multiple percentages to enter, in Composition, set the fabric's fiber composition ratio. First, select the composition. If there are multiple, select them all. Then, enter the percentage in order. Next, enter the weight and thickness as well. Check the information you've entered and click the Compute button. If the draper is connected, measurement will begin. If not, the physical properties will be generated based on the information you entered. You can check the generated result right away in the preview on the left. If you performed tilling in the Map tab beforehand, it will be applied as well. Once generation is complete, you can see the result of a 30cm diameter fabric draped over an 18cm diameter circular plate. Note that the size matches the device's disc and the circular sample size. From the Toggle menu on the left, you can also switch to view a model with 30cm by 30cm square fabric drape as well as a CAPE model. In the Viewer, you can zoom in or out by scrolling the mouse wheel and pan the view by holding down the wheel button while moving the mouse. You can also rotate the view by holding down the right mouse button while moving the mouse. If you'd like to further adjust the fabric's physical properties, click the Advanced Detail menu. However, directly editing the detail properties means changing the result that was generated based on the fabric information. In other words, the properties will change independently of the fabric information you originally entered, so great care is needed when making edits. Once the physical property measurement is complete, click the Upload button in the upper right to save the fabric you've created. In the pop-up window that appears, review the fabric's name, supplier and owner information, and edit the data directly if needed. After confirming the information, click the Go to Closet button. Then, select the upload options for Closet. If you don't want to notify group members with an alert upon upload, enable the first option. If you'd like the following naming rule applied automatically, enable the second option. Since the ZFAB extension doesn't include a custom view, please leave the last option disabled. Next, let's check the ZFAB uploaded to the workroom. A ZFAB uploaded this way can be easily used in Closet software. From the Closet tab in the library, you can select the workroom for the group you uploaded to and try applying it directly to a garment. We hope you'll enjoy easily creating fabrics on the web using Closet. For reference, you can find more information about the ZFAB kit at the ZFAB kit website. For more information, please visit www.closet.com.
markdown_content: ## Overview: Converting Physical Fabric to Digital Fabric in CloSet (CloFab + ZFab kit) This section introduces the CloFab feature in **CloSet** and explains how the **ZFab kit** helps digitize real fabric textures and physical properties into usable digital fabrics. It also covers the fact that web-based digitization can be done without a high-spec PC, and that an image + basic specs can be entered even without owning the equipment. **CloFab** enables creation of high-quality digital fabrics that match real fabrics by using the **ZFab kit**, a dedicated fabric measurement device that precisely scans fabric textures and measures physical properties. Because CloFab runs in a **web browser**, you can digitize fabrics without needing a high-spec PC. Even if you do not own the equipment, you can still create a digital fabric suitable for practical use by entering a **fabric image** you have on hand along with **basic spec information**. --- ## Uploading ZFab Files in CloSet: Workrooms and Permissioned Libraries This section explains how to log into CloSet, choose where the ZFab file should be shared, and upload newly created fabric either directly from CloFab or by starting inside an existing workroom/library. 1. **Log in** with your **CloSet account**. 2. After logging in, select the **group** where you want to share the completed **ZFab** file. There are **two main workflows**: ### Method 1: Start from CloFab menu, then upload to a permissioned workroom - Start digitizing directly through the **CloFab** menu. - When finished, select a **workroom** within the group where you have permission and upload there. - Recommended when you need to upload fabrics to **multiple workrooms**. ### Method 2: Enter a permissioned workroom/library first, then create the fabric - Go to a **workroom** or **company library** where you have permission. - Click **New** at the top and select **Create New Fabric**. - The resulting **ZFab** file uploads directly to that workroom/library. - Recommended when uploading fabrics you worked on consecutively to the **same** workroom or company library. --- ## CloFab Workspace: Fabric Metadata, Map vs Physical Property Tabs This section covers the initial CloFab setup: entering fabric metadata and choosing whether to generate texture maps (Map tab), physical properties (Physical Property tab), or both. ### Enter fabric information - Enter, in order from the top menu: - **Fabric name** - **Supplier** - **Owner information** ### Use the Map and Physical Property tabs - The upper-right area is divided into: - **Map** tab - **Physical Property** tab **Recommended order:** create the **map** first, then measure/generate **physical properties**. If you don’t need a map, you can skip to the **Physical Property** tab and generate only physical properties. --- ## Map Tab: Import Scans or Create Maps with the Scanner This section explains how to load fabric images to generate maps, and how to scan using the closed **ZFabKit** scanner device. ### Map tab buttons 1. **Scan with scanner** - Used when scanning directly with the closed **ZFabKit** scanner device. 2. **Open map** - Import fabric photos without connecting equipment or using previously available files. ### Loading imported maps - Click **Open Map**. - Select the image file(s) (select all you need) and click **Open**. - Use the **map icons** in the toggle menu on the left. - Confirm that the following maps loaded correctly: - **Base color** - **Normal** - **Displacement** - **Roughness** - **Opacity** --- ## ZFabKit Scanner Setup and Status Indicators (Gray/Red/Green) This section describes scanner installation, connection troubleshooting, and calibration flow using the status circle colors in CloFab. ### Scanner connection status - Click **Scan with scanner**. - The connection status updates; check the circle color: - **Gray**: installer not installed - **Red**: ZFab kit not properly connected - **Green**: device ready ### Install installer (if gray) - Click the button to install the installer needed to operate the **ZFab kit**. - After installation, **restart your PC**. ### Connection troubleshooting (if red) - Open **Device Manager** and check that the **ports** and **USB camera** entries match what’s shown on screen. - Example behavior: if both the scanner and draper are connected, the **camera and USB** may appear **twice**. - For detailed troubleshooting, refer to the **FAQ section on the ZFab kit website**. ### Proceed when green - Click the button to move to the next step. --- ## Scanner Calibration: Card Alignment, Duration, and Light Compensation This section explains first-time calibration steps, timing, and why periodic recalibration is needed to avoid color/texture distortion. ### When calibration is required - If operating the device for the first time, you must perform **calibration**. ### Calibration procedure 1. Align the **calibration card** in the center. 2. Ensure the **white colored chip** faces **upper right**. 3. Carefully close the door so the card doesn’t shift. 4. Click the **color checker** button in **Clo-FAB** (CloFab). 5. Calibration takes about **1–2 minutes**. 6. When complete, a **green check** appears. ### After calibration - Remove the calibration card from the tray. - With the tray completely empty, click the **empty** button. - After completion, **Scan fabric with scanner** appears, and the **date of most recent calibration** is shown below it. ### Why recalibrate periodically - Recalibration improves accuracy for **actual fabric color and texture** without distortion. - It compensates for: - Slight device deviations - Changes in surrounding lighting - Especially important if the device has been unused or moved. - If needed, click **calibrate** again. --- ## Scanning Fabric Samples: Size Limits, Placement, and Scan Time This section covers the scanner sample requirements, including maximum scan size, sample preparation, alignment, and scan duration. ### Maximum scan size - Maximum size the device can scan: **32.6 × 21.5 mm** (also stated as **1.6 cm** in the transcript). If the repeating pattern area is large enough, you can prepare a smaller sample than the maximum. ### Sample preparation - Insert the sample into the scanner. - Align with the **grain direction**. - Remove debris/dust from the surface. - Lay the sample flat with **no wrinkles**. ### Start scan - Click **Scan Fabric with Scanner** in CloFab. - Scan time: about **1–2 minutes**. ### Results after scanning - The **base color map** image appears. - A right-side setting menu appears to adjust options. ### Viewer controls - Zoom: mouse wheel. - Pan: hold and move using the wheel. - Hide settings panel: click the **gear-shaped** button. --- ## Saving Original Scan Maps: .zip Export of Per-Map Images This section explains how to save the original scanned images before seamless tiling so they can be reused later. ### Save scan maps (before tiling) - If you want to keep the original scanned image, click **Save Scan Maps**. - Set the file path and click **Save**. ### File format - Saved as a **.zip** file. - After unzipping, you can view the original image for **each map**. ### Important limitation - Saving original images is only possible **at this stage**, so save them now if needed. --- ## Seamless Tiling (Texture Generation): Auto Mode vs Manual Mode This section covers how to generate seamless textures by selecting repeat areas, including automatic pattern detection and manual area blending. ### Tiling mode selection - Use the toggle menu at the top of the **Settings** panel: - **Auto Mode** (toggle ON) - **Manual Mode** (toggle OFF) ### Auto Mode (toggle ON) - Automatically analyzes and finds the most suitable repeat area within the specified range. - Pattern analysis: - Pattern type is **automatically detected by default** (can be changed manually). - **Normal map is required** for accurate pattern type analysis. - Auto mode is only enabled when the **normal map is included**. - Pattern type options: - **Plain irregular**: for fabrics with no distinct patterns or irregular patterns - **Repeat**: for regularly repeating patterns (e.g., checks) ### Auto Mode best practice for accuracy - For automatic tiling, best results are achieved when you select an area that contains repeating patterns **four times**. ### Preview and adjustments - Preview (left) shows: - Original image on the right side - When complete, a **green check** appears. ### After calibration - Remove the calibration card from the tray. - With the tray completely empty, click the **empty** button. - After completion, **Scan fabric with scanner** appears, and the **date of most recent calibration** is shown below it. ### Why recalibrate periodically - Recalibration improves accuracy for **actual fabric color and texture** without distortion. - It compensates for: - Slight device deviations - Changes in surrounding lighting - Especially important if the device has been unused or moved. - If needed, click **calibrate** again. --- ## Scanning Fabric Samples: Size Limits, Placement, and Scan Time This section covers the scanner sample requirements, including maximum scan size, sample preparation, alignment, and scan duration. ### Maximum scan size - Maximum size the device can scan: **32.6 × 21.5 mm** (also stated as **1.6 cm** in the transcript). If the repeating pattern area is large enough, you can prepare a smaller sample than the maximum. ### Sample preparation - Insert the sample into the scanner. - Align with the **grain direction**. - Remove debris/dust from the surface. - Lay the sample flat with **no wrinkles**. ### Start scan - Click **Scan Fabric with Scanner** in CloFab. - Scan time: about **1–2 minutes**. ### Results after scanning - The **base color map** image appears. - A right-side setting menu appears to adjust options. ### Viewer controls - Zoom: mouse wheel. - Pan: hold and move using the wheel. - Hide settings panel: click the **gear-shaped** button. --- ## Saving Original Scan Maps: .zip Export of Per-Map Images This section explains how to save the original scanned images before seamless tiling so they can be reused later. ### Save scan maps (before tiling) - If you want to keep the original scanned image, click **Save Scan Maps**. - Set the file path and click **Save**. ### File format - Saved as a **.zip** file. - After unzipping, you can view the original image for **each map**. ### Important limitation - Saving original images is only possible **at this stage**, so save them now if needed. --- ## Seamless Tiling (Texture Generation): Auto Mode vs Manual Mode This section covers how to generate seamless textures by selecting repeat areas, including automatic pattern detection and manual area blending. ### Tiling mode selection - Use the toggle menu at the top of the **Settings** panel: - **Auto Mode** (toggle ON) - **Manual Mode** (toggle OFF) ### Auto Mode (toggle ON) - Automatically analyzes and finds the most suitable repeat area within the specified range. - Pattern analysis: - Pattern type is **automatically detected by default** (can be changed manually). - **Normal map is required** for accurate pattern type analysis. - Auto mode is only enabled when the **normal map is included**.
